A multinational corporate bank — a Banking & Financial Services engagement delivered by a blended Dataq Software team under the outcome-linked engagement model. Identity withheld as standard; the figures are the client's, reproduced with permission.
Periodic-review files queued for months; analysts spent 70% of their time assembling documents, not judging risk.
Registry extracts, screening results and account history lived across nine systems with no case context. Audit demanded evidence of review rationale; file histories were email archaeology.

Dataq Swarm agents now assemble each review file — registries, screening, financials, relationship notes — under a policy envelope that routes only genuine judgment calls to analysts. The evidence trail (who saw what, when, why) is written as the work happens, and the risk-data spine on Forge keeps customer master data clean enough for the agents to trust.
Outcomes, as the client reported them

items: the agents ran inside a policy envelope with replay, so autonomy never outran the evidence.
one governed definition per metric ended the metric disputes before the build scaled.

blocks.x: If the multinational corporate bank program reads like your own estate, the honest advice is: start with the baseline diagnostic, not with the build. The differences that matter only show up in measurement The engagement model here was build-transfer; the same pattern runs fixed-scope where the estate allows it.
